Hola a todos en el foro, quería iniciar una conversación sobre cómo el entorno digital ha cambiado las reglas de la confianza en las actividades basadas en la fortuna. En el pasado, ver los elementos físicos nos daba una falsa sensación de seguridad, pero hoy en día dependemos de la criptografía и de los generadores de números aleatorios conocidos como RNG. Para muchos usuarios tradicionales, este cambio genera ciertas dudas razonables sobre la transparencia de los resultados. Por eso, considero que es de vital importancia educarnos sobre cómo funcionan estas tecnologías de vanguardia que garantizan que ni la plataforma ni terceros puedan manipular el desenlace de una jugada o de un tiro de dados virtual. La tecnología actual permite un nivel de justicia и verificación que antes era impensable en los salones tradicionales, siempre y cuando elijamos operadores con licencias internacionales respetables. Si desean profundizar en cómo verificar la legitimidad de un sitio de entretenimiento y entender los protocolos de seguridad que protegen a los aficionados hoy en día, los invito a consultar los recursos de https://gamb-loria.net . Aprender a identificar un entorno digital seguro es el primer paso indispensable para disfrutar de la emoción del riesgo con total tranquilidad и confianza. ¿Cómo evalúan la seguridad de un sitio?

By the way, would you extract the variants of the dinosaurs from Dino Crisis 2? (all raptor variants like the purple and green repators, all variants from other species in dino colosseum minigame, etc).

@ziggertron yes! In the Extra Crisis mode—specifically in Dino Duel—alternate colors are assigned to Player 2 if both players select the same dinosaur species. While Player 1 typically uses the primary colors from the main game, Player 2 receives these specific variants: 
Velociraptor: Blue (often referred to as the Ultraraptor in certain versions).
Tyrannosaurus Rex: Black.
Allosaurus: White.
Triceratops: Gray.
Oviraptor: Orange-brown.
Compsognathus: Light green.

Regarding to the raptor, it is the only species with multiple variants in Dino Crisis 2. I found this info:

Main Story Color Variants:
While they all share the same basic model, their colors indicate their "Level" or difficulty:
-Brown (Level 1): The standard, weakest variant encountered at the start of the game.
-Green (Level 2): Feature green skin with orange/brown stripes; they are more resilient than the brown type.
-Swamp Green: A rare, lighter variant with black spots, though similar in strength to standard types.
-Red (Level 5): Encountered late-game (near the Missile Silo). They are significantly more aggressive and have much higher health than brown or green variants.
-Blue (Ultra-Raptor): The strongest non-boss enemy in the game. They only appear if you achieve a 20+ kill combo without taking damage and then enter a new raptor-infested area. They are extremely fast, resistant to hit-stun from the machete or stun gun, and can kill the player in just one or two hits. 

Extra Crisis (Dino Duel) Variants:
Dino Duel mini-game introduces even more colors for mirrors or specific unlocks:
Yellow: A unique variant often associated with specific challenges or the Dino Colosseum.
Black/Alternate Blue: Used primarily to distinguish between Player 1 and Player 2 in versus mode.

I had a PlayStation 1 in the '90s and I used to play Dino Crisis & Dino Crisis 2. I faced some raptor variants in the game, like Blue Raptor, Green Raptor and Red Raptor but I didn't find the other variations. So it will be amazing if you find and extract all of them from the game files!
